title: 1 Small-Cap Stock for Long-Term Investors and 2 We Avoid
content:
Small-cap stocks can be incredibly lucrative investments because their lack of analyst coverage leads to frequent mispricings. However, these businesses (and their stock prices) often stay small because their subscale operations make it harder to expand their competitive moats.

The downside that can come from buying these securities is precisely why we started StockStory - to isolate the long-term winners from the losers so you can invest with confidence. That said, here is one small-cap stock that could be the next big thing and two best left ignored.

Two Small-Cap Stocks to Sell:

DoubleVerify (DV)

Market Cap: $1.69 billion

Using advanced analytics to evaluate over 17 billion digital ad transactions daily, DoubleVerify (NYSE:DV) provides AI-powered technology that verifies digital ads are viewable, fraud-free, brand-suitable, and displayed in the intended geographic location.

Why Do We Think Twice About DV?

Annual revenue growth of 14.3% over the last two years was below our standards for the software sector Customer acquisition costs take a while to recoup, making it difficult to justify sales and marketing investments that could increase revenue Efficiency has decreased over the last year as its operating margin fell by 2 percentage points

At $10.77 per share, DoubleVerify trades at 2.2x forward price-to-sales. If you’re considering DV for your portfolio, see our FREE research report to learn more.

Core Laboratories (CLB)

Market Cap: $759.8 million

With roots dating back to the first commercial oil boom, Core Laboratories (NYSE:CLB) analyzes rock and fluid samples from oil and gas reservoirs to help energy companies optimize production and recovery.

Why Should You Dump CLB?

Muted 1.6% annual revenue growth over the last five years shows its demand lagged behind its energy upstream and integrated energy peers Revenue base of $526.5 million puts it at a disadvantage compared to larger competitors exhibiting economies of scale Gross margin of 20.7% is below its competitors, leaving less money to invest in exploration and production

Core Laboratories is trading at $16.51 per share, or 24.3x forward P/E. Read our free research report to see why you should think twice about including CLB in your portfolio, it’s free.

One Small-Cap Stock to Buy:

Skyward Specialty Insurance (SKWD)

Market Cap: $2.09 billion

Founded in 2006 to serve markets where standard insurance coverage falls short, Skyward Specialty Insurance (NASDAQ:SKWD) provides customized commercial property, casualty, and health insurance solutions for underserved or specialized market niches.

Story Continues

Strong 25.4% annualized net premiums earned expansion over the last two years shows it’s capturing market share this cycle Performance over the past two years shows its incremental sales were extremely profitable, as its annual earnings per share growth of 38.2% outpaced its revenue gains Notable projected book value per share growth of 21.8% for the next 12 months hints at strong capital generation

content:

This is precisely where StockStory comes in - we do the heavy lifting to identify companies with solid fundamentals so you can invest with confidence. Keeping that in mind, here is one stock under $50 with massive upside potential and two that could be down big.

Two Stocks Under $50 to Sell:

QuidelOrtho (QDEL)

Share Price: $14.44

Born from the 2022 merger of Quidel and Ortho Clinical Diagnostics, QuidelOrtho (NASDAQ:QDEL) develops and manufactures diagnostic testing solutions for healthcare providers, from rapid point-of-care tests to complex laboratory instruments and systems.

Why Do We Pass on QDEL?

Weak constant currency growth over the past two years indicates challenges in maintaining its market share Capital intensity has ramped up over the last five years as its free cash flow margin decreased by 21.9 percentage points Eroding returns on capital suggest its historical profit centers are aging

QuidelOrtho’s stock price of $14.44 implies a valuation ratio of 7.1x forward P/E. Check out our free in-depth research report to learn more about why QDEL doesn’t pass our bar.

Hercules Capital (HTGC)

title: Skyward Specialty Insurance Ties USA Rugby Deal To Growth Narrative
content:
Track your investments for FREE with Simply Wall St, the portfolio command center trusted by over 7 million individual investors worldwide.

Skyward Specialty Insurance Group has been named the exclusive insurance partner for all USA Rugby National Teams in a new multi year agreement. The company will also appear as the official front of jersey sponsor, with branding set to debut at upcoming major rugby events. The partnership links NasdaqGS:SKWD to rugby tournaments scheduled in the US, including the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and the 2031 and 2033 Rugby World Cups.

For investors tracking NasdaqGS:SKWD, this sponsorship arrives with the share price at $45.89 and a value score of 4. The stock shows a 4.5% return over the past week and a 117.7% return over three years, while returns over the past year and year to date are negative. That mix of longer term strength and more recent weakness provides context for assessing what this USA Rugby deal could mean for the business.

Pairing the Skyward Specialty Insurance Group brand with global rugby events gives the company visibility in front of new audiences and corporate partners. Readers may want to watch how management uses this agreement for distribution relationships, new product opportunities, and broader brand recognition as these tournaments move closer.

Stay updated on the most important news stories for Skyward Specialty Insurance Group by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio. Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Skyward Specialty Insurance Group.NasdaqGS:SKWD Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Apr 2026

4 things going right for Skyward Specialty Insurance Group that this headline doesn't cover.

This multi year USA Rugby agreement puts Skyward Specialty Insurance Group in front of global audiences at a time when awareness can feed into its specialty property and casualty franchise. As exclusive insurance partner and front of jersey sponsor, Skyward is not just buying logo space; it is tying its brand to tournaments that attract international teams, corporate sponsors, and governing bodies that frequently need complex risk solutions. For a company that already focuses on specialty lines, that exposure can support new distribution relationships and program opportunities if management converts visibility into underwriting partnerships.

How This Fits Into The Skyward Specialty Insurance Group Narrative

The partnership lines up with the narrative that Skyward uses targeted partnerships to access underserved or niche markets, adding another channel where specialized products could be relevant for event organizers, venues, and sponsors. Relying on high profile sponsorships as a gateway to business could add to the concentrated partnership risk already highlighted in the narrative if too much future premium depends on a small set of relationships. The narrative focuses heavily on technology and AI enabled underwriting, while this rugby deal is brand and distribution focused, so any impact on product mix, pricing discipline, or underwriting standards may not yet be fully reflected.

Story Continues

The Risks and Rewards Investors Should Consider

⚠️ Sponsorship costs are not disclosed, so investors have limited visibility on whether the marketing spend will be justified by future premium or fee income. ⚠️ If returns from this partnership are slower than expected, it could feed into the existing concern about concentrated partnerships and execution risk around new distribution channels. 🎁 The deal can support brand recognition just as Skyward prepares to report first quarter 2026 results and integrates Apollo Group Holdings, giving the company more ways to introduce its specialty offerings to potential clients. 🎁 Aligning with major tournaments ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and the 2031 and 2033 Rugby World Cups could help Skyward position itself alongside larger insurers such as Chubb, AIG, or Travelers in conversations around complex event and liability coverage.

What To Watch Going Forward

From here, watch for concrete signs that this sponsorship is doing more than raising brand awareness. That includes any commentary on new program launches tied to sports or events, references on earnings calls to rugby related distribution, or early cross selling opportunities as Apollo Group Holdings is consolidated. Share price performance has recently weakened despite positive multi year returns, so investors may also track how management frames this agreement during the May 2026 results call and whether analysts start to reference the partnership when discussing growth, underwriting quality, or marketing efficiency.

title: Skyward Specialty Insurance Group to Host First Quarter 2026 Earnings Call Thursday, May 7th, 2026
content:
Skyward Specialty Insurance Group, Inc.

HOUSTON , April 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Skyward Specialty Insurance Group, Inc (Nasdaq: SKWD) (“Skyward Group” or “the Company”), expects to issue its first quarter 2026 earnings, inclusive of Apollo Group Holdings Ltd., after market close on Wednesday, May 6th which will be available on the Company website at investors.skywardinsurance.com under Quarterly Results.

Focused on the specialty industry’s most niche, complex risks of today and the emerging challenges of tomorrow, Skyward Group leverages the forward-looking insight and disciplined execution of each organization to drive sustainable growth and long-term value for its shareholders, distribution partners, and other stakeholders.

title: Why Skyward (SKWD) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again
content:
Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Skyward Specialty Insurance (SKWD), which belongs to the Zacks Insurance - Property and Casualty industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

This property and casualty insurance holding company has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 22.70%.

For the most recent quarter, Skyward was expected to post earnings of $0.96 per share, but it reported $1.17 per share instead, representing a surprise of 21.88%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $0.85 per share, while it actually produced $1.05 per share, a surprise of 23.53%.

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for Skyward. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Skyward has an Earnings ESP of +8.41% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner.

Investors should note, however, that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss, but a negative value does reduce the predictive power of this metric.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, but that may not be the sole basis for their stocks moving higher. On the other hand, some stocks may hold their ground even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Because of this, it's really important to check a company's Earnings ESP ahead of its quarterly release to increase the odds of success. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.
